steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to enable component creation and state management.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, setting up the foundation for building a component with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main FileStorageSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named FileStorageSystem that returns null initially.
steps.hint: Define a component using either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should return null for now.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the FileStorageSystem component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A FileStorageSystem component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The component is named FileStorageSystem and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main component structure for the file storage system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'FileStorageSystem' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and that it returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for file list
steps.instruction: Inside your FileStorageSystem component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'files' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty array [] as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for a list of items
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a 'files' state variable ready to store file objects, initialized as an empty array.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that creates a 'files' state variable initialized to an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized state to manage the collection of files in the storage system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] as the initial value and naming the state variable 'files'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization isn't quite right. Use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'files' with an empty array as its initial value.

steps.title: Initialize state for selected file
steps.instruction: Inside the FileStorageSystem component, use useState to create a state variable called selectedFile initialized to null.
steps.hint: Add a new useState call after the existing files state. The initial value should be null.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state for tracking a selected item
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a selectedFile state variable ready to track which file is currently selected.
successCriteria: selectedFile state is declared using useState with an initial value of null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added state to track the selected file. This will allow the UI to highlight or show details for a specific file later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a selectedFile variable initialized to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to add a new state variable called selectedFile with an initial value of null.

steps.title: Define the addFile handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your FileStorageSystem component, define a function named addFile that takes a parameter (e.g., fileData) and uses setFiles to add that new file to the files state array.
steps.hint: The addFile function should update the files state by creating a new array that includes all existing files plus the new file data.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an addFile function that can be used to add new files to the files state.
successCriteria: The addFile function is defined, takes a parameter, and uses setFiles to update the state with the new file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the addFile handler function. This function will allow users to add new files to the storage system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your addFile function properly updates the files state using setFiles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addFile function is not defined correctly. Check that it takes a parameter and updates the files state array.

steps.title: Define the selectFile handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your FileStorageSystem component, define a function named selectFile that takes a file object as a parameter and updates the selectedFile state to that file.
steps.hint: You can create an arrow function or a regular function. Use setSelectedFile to update the state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A selectFile function is defined that updates the selectedFile state when called with a file object.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named selectFile that accepts a parameter and calls setSelectedFile with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the selectFile handler. This function will allow users to select a file from the list.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your selectFile function accepts a parameter and calls setSelectedFile with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectFile function isn't defined correctly. It should take a file parameter and update the selectedFile state using setSelectedFile.

steps.title: Define the removeFile handler function
steps.instruction: Define a function named removeFile that takes a file name as a parameter and removes that file from the files state array.
steps.hint: Use the setFiles function to update the state by filtering out the file with the matching name.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a removeFile function that filters the files state to exclude the specified file name.
successCriteria: The removeFile function is defined, takes a file name parameter, and uses setFiles with a filter to remove that file from the state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the removeFile handler function that will delete files from the storage system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your removeFile function properly filters the files array using the file name parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeFile function isn't defined correctly. It should take a file name and update the files state by filtering out that file.

steps.title: Add the main container structure
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your FileStorageSystem component, replace the existing div with a new div that has className 'file-storage-system' and contains two main sections.
steps.hint: Create a parent div with the specified className and add two empty section elements inside it.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: a container with two sections
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a structured container with two main sections ready for file storage UI elements.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div with className 'file-storage-system' that has two section elements inside it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main container structure for the file storage interface.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have exactly two section elements inside the div with className 'file-storage-system'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The structure doesn't match the requirements. Check that you have a div with className 'file-storage-system' containing two section elements.

steps.title: Create the file list display section
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your FileStorageSystem component, add a <section> element with className 'file-list' that maps through the files state to display each file.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the files array to generate a list of elements. Each file object in the array can be displayed in a <div> or <li>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A section element with the class 'file-list' is added to the component's return statement, ready to display the list of files.
successCriteria: The component returns a <section> element with className 'file-list' that contains a map expression over the files state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the file list display section. This will be the container for showing all files in the storage system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a <section> element with className 'file-list' and are mapping through the files state inside it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file list display section is missing or incomplete. Please add a <section> element with className 'file-list' that maps through the files state.

steps.title: Create the file details display section
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add a section element with className 'file-details' that displays information about the selected file. Use conditional rendering to only show this section when a file is selected.
steps.hint: Add a <section> element with the className 'file-details'. Inside it, use a ternary operator to check if selectedFile exists, then display file details like name and size.
steps.expectedOutcome: A file details section appears in the UI that shows information about the selected file when one is selected, and displays a fallback message when no file is selected.
successCriteria: The component contains a <section> element with className 'file-details' that uses conditional rendering to display selected file information or a fallback message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the file details section with proper conditional rendering.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the section, but make sure to include conditional rendering that checks if selectedFile exists and displays appropriate content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file details section is missing or incomplete. Add a <section> with className 'file-details' that conditionally displays file information.

steps.title: Add file list items with selection wiring
steps.instruction: Inside the file list map, create div elements for each file with onClick wired to selectFile.
steps.hint: Map over the files array and return a div for each file. Use the file's id or name as a key and set onClick to call selectFile with that file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The file list will display each file as a clickable div that triggers the selectFile handler when clicked.
successCriteria: A map function is used to iterate over the files array
Each file is rendered as a div element
Each div has an onClick handler that calls selectFile with the file object
Each div has a unique key prop
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created interactive file list items that can be selected by clicking.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each file div has an onClick handler that calls selectFile with the file object and includes a unique key prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file list items aren't properly wired for selection. Remember to map over the files array and create div elements with onClick handlers that call selectFile.

steps.title: Add file management controls
steps.instruction: Add a 'Add Sample File' button and a 'Remove Selected File' button inside the main container, wiring their onClick handlers to the addFile and removeFile functions respectively.
steps.hint: Place two button elements with appropriate labels and onClick handlers that call your existing handler functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the UI: one to add sample files and another to remove the selected file, both wired to their respective handler functions.
successCriteria: The component contains an 'Add Sample File' button with onClick={addFile} and a 'Remove Selected File' button with onClick={removeFile}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added file management controls. The buttons are properly wired to handle file operations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but check that both required buttons are present with correct onClick handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file management controls are missing or incorrectly implemented. Ensure you add both buttons with proper onClick wiring.
